Rule.name: fixed-persian-01-01
Rule.comment: The Persian New Year. Falls on 1 Farvardin, the day containing the vernal equinox at the central meridian of Iran (typically 20 or 21 March). Officially observed as a public holiday in Iran, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Azerbaijan, and other Central Asian and Caucasian states with Persian cultural heritage, and recognised by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The 13-day duration captures the traditional Nowruz holiday period, which culminates in Sizdah Bedar (Nature's Day) on 13 Farvardin.

Rule.name: fixed-persian-01-13
Rule.comment: Nature's Day. The thirteenth and final day of the Nowruz holiday period, observed on 13 Farvardin. Traditionally celebrated by spending the day outdoors with family, picnicking, and disposing of the sabzeh (sprouted greens) from the Haft-sin Nowruz table by casting it into running water. A public holiday in Iran and recognised in other Persian-cultural-heritage countries.

Rule.name: fixed-persian-09-30
Rule.comment: Shab-e Yalda, the longest night of the year. Observed on 30 Azar — the last day of the autumn season, immediately preceding the winter solstice. Traditionally celebrated by family gatherings that last past midnight, with readings from the poetry of Hafez, the eating of pomegranates and watermelons, and the lighting of candles. The Gregorian date falls on 20 or 21 December depending on the year. Not a public holiday but one of the most widely observed cultural observances in Iran and across Persian-heritage communities. Anchored to the calendar day on which the longest night begins.
